HOLY SHIT. This is like asking how computer chips are designed. Long story short- it is really complicated. Everyone who has a drivers license thinks she is qualified to design roads, like everyone who uses a computers thinks he could design a computer chip. Neither group could design anything.

There's as many types of traffic light timings as there there are computer chips- more traffic light types probably. And chip designers don't have to worry about 10 independent layers of bureaucracy from city, county, state, and federal groups- or input from "concerned citizens" who just want the light by their houses to turn faster. Guess what? Everybody wants their damn light timings to be faster, but the traffic engineer has to accommodate all traffic light requests simultaneously. Changing any one of them, influences the strain and pressures on every other traffic light in a network simultaneously- usually in bizarre and unforeseen ways. This phenomena is especially amazing on networks that don't have coordination and the various lights each work with independent time programing.

1st the engineers take a traffic count, usually those tubes you see stretched across the road at important nodal points.

2nd they decide if there will be left turns, what type of left turns, what priority will be given to left turns, how much protection will left turns have. Will there be signal actuation from crosswalks, in-ground traffic queue senors, emergency vehicles, transit vehicles prioritization, and about 10 thousand other little detail- each of which drastically increases network delay.

3rd they decide how much they care about side street traffic.

4th they build very complex origin\destination matrices to prioritize travel times between different parts of the network.

5th they hope they have reasonable estimates of traffic patters throughout the entire network (considering patterns change per day, per hour, per special event like sports matches or school getting out).

6th they build complex computer simulations to validate their estimates of traffic patterns.

7th they construct sophisticated genetic algorithms to optimize traffic signals, with the best patterns becoming the parents for future generations of simulation inputs.

8th they calibrate and validate their findings.

9th they hope they have reasonable signal timings and present their findings to untrained city councils and the public who don't trust a single word or calculation a traffic engineer presents- because again they have drivers licenses and know better god dammit! Imagine if the public and elected representatives got to mandate how structural engineers design bridges or skyscrapers.
